headline_marked: 115 charges: [[Man City found guilty of financial fraud]]
headline: 115 charges: Man City found guilty of financial fraud
summary: The Premier League leaders face severe sanctions, including potential relegation and the loss of titles, after being found guilty of widespread financial breaches.
details: Manchester City have been found guilty of widespread financial fraud across a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018, according to a Premier League statement.
The club was found guilty on almost all of the 115 charges they faced, following a case that began with leaked documents in 2018.
Potential sanctions include a hefty points penalty that could lead to relegation, a massive fine, or even expulsion from the Premier League.
There is also speculation that the club could be stripped of titles and trophies won during the period of the breaches.
Manchester City have announced their intent to appeal the decision, with Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak expressing confidence in proving the club's innocence.
The final outcome remains uncertain as the club may also seek redress in England's High Court regarding the arbitration process.
Rival clubs and figures, such as Rio Ferdinand, have reacted with anticipation of the potential fallout and the impact on the league's standings.
caption:
Man City found guilty of almost all 115 financial fraud charges. Relegation or stripped titles could be next.

Manchester City have been found guilty of widespread financial fraud across a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018, according to a Premier League statement.

The club was found guilty on almost all of the 115 charges they faced, following a case that began with leaked documents in 2018.

Potential sanctions include a hefty points penalty that could lead to relegation, a massive fine, or even expulsion from the Premier League.

There is also speculation that the club could be stripped of titles and trophies won during the period of the breaches.

Manchester City have announced their intent to appeal the decision, with Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak expressing confidence in proving the club's innocence.

The final outcome remains uncertain as the club may also seek redress in England's High Court regarding the arbitration process.

Rival clubs and figures, such as Rio Ferdinand, have reacted with anticipation of the potential fallout and the impact on the league's standings.

headline_marked: Yamal shines as [[Spain hammer Croatia 4-1]] in Nations League
headline: Yamal shines as Spain hammer Croatia 4-1 in Nations League
summary: Lamine Yamal scored twice and provided an assist to lead the World Cup champions to a dominant victory in their first home game since lifting the trophy.
details: Lamine Yamal scored two goals and set up another as Spain defeated Croatia 4-1 on Tuesday in the Nations League. The match was Spain's first home game since winning the World Cup.
The 19-year-old Yamal opened the scoring within 75 seconds of kick-off with a left-footed finish, taking his international goal tally to nine in 36 appearances.
Croatia equalized shortly before the 30-minute mark through a Dion Beljo header from an Ivan Perisic cross.
Spain quickly restored their lead two minutes later when Marc Pubill scored a header from a pin-point cross by Yamal.
Yamal claimed his second goal after 63 minutes, beating goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic at the near post.
Nico Williams added a fourth goal with a crisp dribble and finish in the final two minutes of the match.
The victory extends Spain's unbeaten run to 40 matches, including their final triumph over Argentina in June.
Before the match, Captain Rodri displayed the World Cup trophy at the packed Estadio Ramon Sanchez-Pizjuan.
caption:
Lamine Yamal's brilliance leads Spain to a 4-1 rout of Croatia!

Lamine Yamal scored two goals and set up another as Spain defeated Croatia 4-1 on Tuesday in the Nations League. The match was Spain's first home game since winning the World Cup.

The 19-year-old Yamal opened the scoring within 75 seconds of kick-off with a left-footed finish, taking his international goal tally to nine in 36 appearances.

Croatia equalized shortly before the 30-minute mark through a Dion Beljo header from an Ivan Perisic cross.

Spain quickly restored their lead two minutes later when Marc Pubill scored a header from a pin-point cross by Yamal.

Yamal claimed his second goal after 63 minutes, beating goalkeeper Dominik Livakovic at the near post.

Nico Williams added a fourth goal with a crisp dribble and finish in the final two minutes of the match.

The victory extends Spain's unbeaten run to 40 matches, including their final triumph over Argentina in June.

Before the match, Captain Rodri displayed the World Cup trophy at the packed Estadio Ramon Sanchez-Pizjuan.
